evals.prompt: animate this site, make it feel alive. it's a static html site for a plumber, files are in the site folder. don't add any frameworks
evals.expected_output: The reply lists a page inventory. Signals land only on matching elements: press on the two buttons, focus-glow on the inputs, submit-states on the form button, field-error wiring, nav-underline on the nav, card-lift on the two link cards but not the licence card, count-up on the three stats but not the pricing table, section-reveal on below-fold sections but not the hero, headline-emphasis on the H1, drop-answer only if the file input is turned into a dropzone. Nothing on the pricing table or footer. signals.css and signals.js land in css/ and js/, not a new folder. Tokens set to the site's teal, not the demo teal. No React, no library. Reply names what was left out and the source.
assertions: index.html does not put data-sig-reveal on the hero section or the header
The licence card (the div.card that is not a link) does not have class sig-card
No pricing table cell has data-sig-count
signals.css is linked from css/ and signals.js from js/ (no new top-level folder)
No <script> tag loads React, Vue, Motion, GSAP or any CDN library
The reply text contains an inventory and a line naming what was deliberately left out
--sig-accent in the shipped signals.css is not #2dd4bf

evals.prompt: the upload box on the client portal does nothing when you drag a file over it, and when the upload fails you just get a red 'error' and have to start again. make it feel like a real app
evals.expected_output: drop-answer on the dropzone, honest-progress with percent, time left and rate, inline-retry with the file kept and resume from where it stopped, upload-preview after success. Nothing added elsewhere on the page. Reply names the reel as the source.
assertions: The dropzone element gains data-sig-dropzone and a sig-swap with idle and over copy
The progress element uses scaleX via --p, not width
A retry control exists inside the progress element with data-retry
No other element on the page gained a sig- class or data-sig- attribute

evals.prompt: can you add some motion to the pricing table and the footer links, the page feels flat
evals.expected_output: Push back: the pricing table is data people read and the footer links are low-frequency navigation, neither takes a signal from this catalogue. Offer the signals that do fit the rest of the page instead (nav-underline for the primary nav, press on the CTA, section-reveal on the sections that are below the fold), and say plainly that the table and footer were left alone and why.
assertions: No sig- class or data-sig- attribute is added to the table or its cells
No sig- class or data-sig- attribute is added to footer links
The reply says the table and footer were left alone and gives the reason
